summary: Observation of a stationary luminous phenomenon beneath dark clouds, followed by rapid movement towards the clouds. No noise, no trail: unexplained, moderately consistent phenomenon.
description: Observation made in November 1963 by three witnesses and reported to GEIPAN in April 2008. On November 11, 1963, around 3 or 4 p.m., a father and his two sons (aged 18 and 13) were walking along a country path when they observed a luminous phenomenon that intrigued them. An orange sphere of light remained stationary below dark clouds for over a minute. Afterward, it began rotating, oscillating from right to left for a few seconds before disappearing at very high speed into the clouds along a straight, upward-curving trajectory. No noise or trail was observed. No other accounts of this phenomenon were reported. The details of the event were gradually reconstructed between 2003 and 2007 by one of the witnesses (the 18-year-old student). The hypothesis of observing ball lightning (plasma) was refuted because, firstly, the witness did not confirm the presence of a thunderstorm during the family walk, and secondly, there were differences in characteristics between the phenomenon observed on November 11, 1963, and those known to describe ball lightning. GEIPAN classifies this case as D1: unexplained phenomenon, moderately consistent (single testimony, old and distant occurrence) but with a marked strangeness.
